summary: The kpool ragged plan path ignored its chunk predicate and requested one dense fp32 logits matrix across all query and pooled-KV rows. The candidate now chunks query rows under a bounded free/total-memory budget while preserving the fitting fast path.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before evidence: 5 failed, 1 passed; the forced two-row budget still produced one MQA-logits call rather than three. Raw output: regression_before.log
6 passed, including production-shape budget arithmetic, small/large/zero-memory boundaries, and GPU plan-path dense-vs-chunked dispatch/padding equivalence. Raw output: regression_after.log
3 existing non-kpool budget boundary tests passed. Raw output: existing_budget_test.log
No whitespace errors. Raw output: diff_check.log

gpu_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X/gfx950 with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015. The regression allocated fp8 and metadata tensors on the GPU and exercised the actual plan orchestration; DeepGEMM/top-k were mocked.
remaining_limitations: No GLM-5.3-Flash or RadixArk weights were available.
The reported 4x B300 CUDA/TP serving workload and prefix-cache traffic were not reproduced on the single AMD GPU.
NVIDIA DeepGEMM allocation behavior and end-to-end model semantic accuracy remain unverified locally.
A broader open upstream candidate, PR 38469, additionally splits the concatenated K layout per request; this PR intentionally implements only the independently validated query-row allocation bound.
